rule: James, 11 November 2026: no opening-review item for a skill students in the course already have, or that only Challenge or Exam questions need.

removed.reason: Vertically opposite angles and angles on a straight line are Year 7 content that Stage 4 students have just met and the booklet's own earlier lesson covers, so it is not a commonly missing skill.

content.prompt: Calculate the value of $a$ and $b$. Give a brief reason.

answer.worked:
$a=65^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles are equal)
$$\begin{align*}b+65&=180\\b&=115^\circ\end{align*}$$
(angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$)

classification.difficultyReason: Two direct applications: vertically opposite angles, then a straight line, with a brief reason.

removed.reason: Angles at a point summing to 360° is taught in Stage 4 angle work just before this lesson, and the audit only called it unstated, so it is an assumed skill.

answer.worked:
Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}x+70+60&=360\\x+130&=360\\x&=230^\circ\end{align*}$$

classification.difficultyReason: One equation, but the student must see that x is the reflex sector and use the 360° sum.
